_schema: known-findings v1 (HIMMEL-2058). One entry per recurring CR finding CLASS. `kind`: fix = a real defect class with a canonical fix; rebuttal = a false-premise class with a canonical rebuttal (critics are told not to re-raise it unless the code regressed); checklist = a judgment class the self-review asks about. `detector` runs in scripts/cr/known-findings.sh --diff (deterministic, no LLM): added-line-regex = POSIX-ERE over ADDED lines of files matching `globs`; twin-missing = a .sh/.ps1 twin exists but is not in the diff; no-test-change = non-test sources under `globs` changed and no test-*.sh/*.test.* file did; removed-flag-in-docs = a `--flag` token deleted from source still appears in a doc that also names that source file; md-fence-no-lang = an added ``` fence with no language in a .md; hook-header-no-fail-direction = a NEW scripts/hooks/*.sh whose header never states fail-open/fail-closed; files under a testdata/ dir are fixture data and never scanned. `learning_match` is the regex --refresh uses to attribute CodeRabbit learnings-export rows (sums their Usage into evidence.learnings_uses). `evidence.ledger` is rewritten by --refresh from the CR ledger (findings whose file matches `globs`, verdicts resolved through amends). Hand-edit everything else; keep ids stable (they are cited in PR comments).

classes.title: errexit hazards claimed in scripts that do not (or do not relevantly) use set -e
classes.canonical: House style is `set -uo pipefail` WITHOUT errexit (shell-lint flags `set -e` itself). In a file that does not enable errexit, an errexit-interaction finding has no premise. In a file that DOES set -e: a failing command in a NON-FINAL position of an `&&` list is exempt; bare `wait` (no operand) returns 0 even when jobs failed; `rm -f <missing-path>` succeeds. Reply with the file's prologue line and the construct's actual status, then mark disproved.
classes.coverage: .coderabbit.yaml path_instructions cover NON-errexit files only; the errexit-file carve-out is HIMMEL-1684 (open). CodeRabbit learnings (3 entries, ~1.8k uses) suppress most re-raises in practice: 2 App re-raises since 2026-08-10, one of them legitimate (a `set -e` caller).

classes.title: leading-zero operands: decimal in `[ ]`, octal only in arithmetic contexts
classes.canonical: `[ "$a" -gt "$b" ]` compares digit strings as DECIMAL — leading zeros (`date +%m` = 08) never trigger octal there; disprove. Only `$(( ))`, `(( ))` and `let` are octal contexts: there, normalise an operand that can carry a leading zero (date fields, env/user input) with `$((10#$var))` — that is the one legitimate fix in this class.
classes.coverage: .coderabbit.yaml path_instructions (bracket-decimal rule) + learning (552 uses). The 2 App re-raises since 2026-08-10 were both real arithmetic-context cases on env input, so the detector only flags arithmetic on env-shaped (UPPERCASE) operands without 10#.

classes.title: handover-path.sh / handover_root demanded of a script that touches no handover path
classes.canonical: The scripts/handover/CLAUDE.md rule (source scripts/lib/handover-path.sh, call handover_root) binds a script that READS, WRITES or RESOLVES handover state at runtime. A pure test, a helper that only mentions scripts/handover/ in a comment, a hook that pattern-matches the string 'handovers/', and BRIDGE_ROOT lane-session state (a different root) are out of scope — disprove with one line naming what the script actually touches. Four sub-shapes recur, and all are out of scope unless the script itself resolves handover state: (a) TRANSITIVE — the script only invokes another script that resolves the root (handover-bridge.sh -> append-cr-findings.sh); (b) REPO_ROOT — deriving a checkout root is not handover state (test-machine-setup-hermetic.sh); (c) 'resolves or creates filesystem paths' / Git common-directory state, which is CR-ledger state under .git, not handover state (panel-first-pass.sh, git-show-safe.sh); (d) the BLANKET form, 'add the bootstrap to every new or modified shell script', which carries no premise at all. The detector flags the opposite, real defect: a literal handovers/ path built in a script instead of handover_root.
classes.coverage: .coderabbit.yaml handover-root carve-out covers a test that redirects HANDOVER_DIR but not a test that touches no handover path (HIMMEL-1684 gap 2, open). Still the single most-raised class in the measured window despite being the #1 learning: 8 App raises across 6 PRs, hand-counted over 2026-08-20..09-02 (a subset of the since-08-10 field above, which this refresh therefore raises from 3 to 8 as a measured lower bound), and CodeRabbit WITHDREW every one on rebuttal. The learning is applied 1009 times yet does not suppress the raise — which is why the rebuttal now enumerates the four sub-shapes instead of restating the rule.

classes.title: bare `mktemp` / `mktemp -d` without a template (BSD/macOS portability)
classes.canonical: Use `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<name>.XXXXXX"` (or `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<name>.XXXXXX"`), and capture its failure before building paths on the result. Same regex as shell-lint [mktemp].
classes.coverage: shell-lint [mktemp] (advisory; only catches it when shell-lint is actually run) + .coderabbit.yaml portability rule. 6 App re-raises since 2026-08-10 — every one a real bare call in a NEW test suite, i.e. the rule exists but was not run pre-panel; that is the gap this step closes. Note the learnings store holds two CONTRADICTING entries (220 uses: template required; 75 uses: bare -d works on macOS) — the house rule is the template.

classes.title: GNU-only command or flag in cross-platform shell (timeout, find -maxdepth, sed -i, date -d, readlink -f, grep -P, \s, hardcoded /usr/bin/cat)
classes.canonical: Scripts run on Git Bash, macOS (bash 3.2, BSD userland) and Linux. Pair a GNU flag with its BSD alternative on the same line, use the repo's resolver for `timeout` (source scripts/lib/timeout-bin.sh, then `${_TIMEOUT_BIN:+"$_TIMEOUT_BIN" N} cmd` -- bound-only calls run unbounded without it, hang-guard rows SKIP), prefer `[[:space:]]` over `\s`, Bash file tests over `find -maxdepth`, and mark a deliberate GNU-only line with `# gnu-ok: <why>`. Never hardcode an absolute /usr/bin/<coreutil> path for a utility macOS keeps in /bin instead: /usr/bin/cat is ENOENT there — invoke the bare name and let PATH resolve it, or resolve once with command -v. Utilities macOS keeps in /usr/bin (sed, awk, grep, head, tail, cut, sort, find, stat) are deliberately NOT flagged — /usr/bin/sed is not a portability bug there. BSD grep also lacks BRE \| alternation: use grep -E with a plain |.
classes.coverage: shell-lint GNU_FLAG_PAT + PCRE_CLASS cover sed/date/readlink/grep -P/stat/\s; bare `timeout N` and `find -maxdepth` were NOT covered (3+ App re-raises each since 2026-08-10) — this detector adds them. 20 App re-raises in the class since 2026-08-10 (largest real-defect class). 2026-09-02 refresh: 3 further portability raises in the window — /usr/bin/cat absent on macOS (CodeRabbit App finding, PR #2107: "/usr/bin/cat does not exist on macOS; macOS ships cat at /bin/cat only" — the only /usr/bin/<coreutil> entry this detector asserts, deliberately; the list grows one evidenced finding at a time rather than from an unverified enumeration of the macOS /bin layout), a GNU-only hard-link identity check, and BSD grep \| alternation (the latter two prose-only, no detector).

classes.title: bash 4+ construct (mapfile/readarray, declare -A, ${v,,}, |&, &>>)
classes.canonical: Use a `while IFS= read -r` loop instead of mapfile, parallel indexed arrays or case tables instead of associative arrays, `tr` for case folding, `2>&1 |` / `>> f 2>&1` for the bash-4 redirection shorthands.
classes.coverage: shell-lint BASH32 + .coderabbit.yaml path_instructions; 2 App re-raises since 2026-08-10.

classes.title: a .sh/.ps1 twin changed without its counterpart
classes.canonical: Same-named .sh/.ps1 pairs are behavioural twins: change both in lockstep, or say in the PR why the twin is unaffected. Standalone .ps1 files (no .sh twin) carry no parity duty.
classes.coverage: .coderabbit.yaml **/*.ps1 instruction tells CodeRabbit to flag drift — nothing checks it BEFORE the panel. 5 App re-raises since 2026-08-10; learnings 91 + 8 + 3 uses.

classes.title: UTF-8 BOM: required on a non-ASCII .ps1, an error on any .sh
classes.canonical: Windows PowerShell 5.1 decodes a no-BOM UTF-8 .ps1 as cp1252, so a .ps1 with non-ASCII bytes MUST carry a UTF-8 BOM (HIMMEL-1432); a shell file must NOT (breaks the shebang, SC1082). A 'repository no-BOM convention for .ps1' claim is a stale learning (91 uses, pre-1432) — disprove by citing shell-lint [PS1-NO-BOM].
classes.coverage: shell-lint [BOM] / [PS1-NO-BOM] / [PS1-ENCODING]; 0 App re-raises since 2026-08-10. Kept so nobody 'fixes' toward the stale learning.

classes.title: source changed, no test changed
classes.canonical: Every new flag, branch and exit code in the diff gets a case in the paired suite (`test-<name>.sh` beside the script, or the *.test.* file); assert the behaviour, not the stub. If the change is genuinely untestable here, say so in the PR body so the panel does not ask.
classes.coverage: No structural check — 16 App re-raises since 2026-08-10 (and the pragmatist critic lens names it); the biggest judgment class.

classes.title: a removed/renamed `--flag` is still documented
classes.canonical: For every identifier, flag, exit code or path the diff removes or renames, grep docs/, README.md, CLAUDE.md and the command runbooks and update the prose in the same PR (doc-freshness step 2.7 only covers the mapped pairs).
classes.coverage: doc-freshness advise rows cover a handful of mapped source→doc pairs; 21 App re-raises since 2026-08-10 were stale/contradicting prose — the single largest CodeRabbit class now.

classes.title: `<producer> | grep -q` under `set -o pipefail` (early exit SIGPIPEs the producer; a negated guard inverts)
classes.canonical: With pipefail, `grep -q` exits on the first match, the producer takes SIGPIPE writing the rest, and the PIPELINE status is non-zero — so `if ! cmd | grep -q …` flips on large inputs and a successful match can read as failure (HIMMEL-1430). Capture instead: `out=$(cmd | grep -E …); [ -n "$out" ]`, or `grep -q … <<< "$small"` for inputs well under 64 KiB (larger here-strings wedge Git Bash, HIMMEL-2027). Mark a deliberate pipe with `# pipefail-ok: <why>`.
classes.coverage: No structural check; shell-lint does not flag it. Raised by the panel on this very PR (round 4 codex-1) and previously on test-cr-tune.sh (HIMMEL-1430) — added to the catalogue from the refresh loop this PR introduces.

classes.title: jq's `//` swallows `false` as well as `null` — use has()/type for presence, not `// empty`
classes.canonical: jq's `//` treats `false` exactly like `null`, so `.field // empty` is NOT a presence test — it silently swallows a legitimate `false`, and the caller takes the absent branch while reporting success. Ask the question you mean: presence -> `has("field")`; presence plus a type contract -> `(.field | type) == "string"` (better than has(), because it also rejects malformed values); a value that may legitimately be false -> read it explicitly, `if has("f") then (.f|tostring) else "absent" end`. Do NOT over-correct into treating ANY present value as the signal: on #2071 that flipped a malformed payload (true / 123 / {}) into a DENY, and a fail-open workflow guard must ALLOW on an unreadable payload. Key the fix on the field's documented contract, not on 'stop using //'. Mark a deliberate benign default with `# jq-alt-ok: <why>`.
classes.coverage: No structural check; shell-lint does not parse jq filters. The detector is deliberately NARROW — restricted to boolean-ish field names — because the broad `.field // (empty|"")` form matches 147 lines repo-wide (293 raw `// empty` occurrences), nearly all legitimate string defaults; a detector that fires on every PR buries the signal. Measured cost of the narrow form: 5 repo-wide hits, 3 of them in files that document this very trap. Ratified as a class by the 01R console 2026-09-01 (HIMMEL-2361). CR round 3 removed a `| type` clause from this exclude: it was unnecessary — the safe spelling `(.f | type) == "string"` carries no `//`, so the main pattern never matched it anyway — and, being a WHOLE-LINE match, it silently suppressed the genuinely buggy `.f // empty | type`, which still swallows false. The sibling `has(` clause has the same whole-line shape and may suppress a true positive too (`if has("f") then .f // empty` still swallows false: has() establishes presence, it does not stop `//` treating false as absent); that one is NOT removed here because it may cover a real safe form — tracked for verification in HIMMEL-2453.

sightings: scripts/hooks/block-subagent-park.sh — `.agent_id // empty` read a payload carrying "agent_id": false as ABSENT, so the guard silently did not fire: fail-open and invisible (HIMMEL-2140, PR #2071, CodeRabbit round 1). Fixed to (.agent_id | type) == "string".
scripts/machine-setup/test-machine-setup-hermetic.sh — an autoupdate_true helper would have reported a seeded autoUpdate: false as absent, mis-grading a parity case (HIMMEL-2353 / 2356).

scripts/hooks/orchestrator-inline-guard.sh:186 — live `.agent_id // empty`, documented as fail-SAFE there (an unrecognised value merely declines to exempt a worker): a sighting to document, NOT a defect to patch.

classes.title: non-ASCII literal inside a grep/sed/awk bracket expression never matches under the default locale — use an alternation
classes.canonical: A bracket expression containing a multi-byte literal (em dash U+2014, arrows, box-drawing) is locale-dependent: under Git Bash with LANG unset the class silently never matches, so the guard is green forever. Measured on the repo's own skip marker `<name>: SKIPPED — 0 cases ran`: `[—-]` matched nothing while the alternation `(—|-)` matched the same line (HIMMEL-2359, PR #2070). Spell it as an alternation — ERE `(—|-)`, BRE `\(—\|-\)` — or match the byte sequence under LC_ALL=C, or normalise the text first. The same trap bites the matcher you write to FIND this bug: PCRE `[\x80-\xff]` under a UTF-8 locale is a CODEPOINT class U+0080-U+00FF and so cannot match U+2014 — run that sweep under LC_ALL=C, and positive-control it on a planted line before trusting a zero. Mark a deliberate non-ASCII class with `# non-ascii-ok: <why>`.
classes.coverage: No structural check; shellcheck does not model locale-dependent bracket expressions. Tree sweep 2026-09-02 (LC_ALL=C, positive-controlled): 0 real occurrences — the 26 apparent file hits are all prose comments and JSON string literals, not matcher bracket expressions, which is why the detector is scoped to a grep/sed/awk/=~ context rather than to any `[...]`. Same family as HIMMEL-2236 (pwsh_unicode awk %c locale). Detector-flavour note: `added-line-regex` patterns are compiled by `ere()` in known-findings.sh — POSIX class names ([:space:], [:alnum:], [:alpha:], [:digit:]) are substituted, then the result is handed to JavaScript's `new RegExp`. That is the ONLY consumer of `detector.pattern`; nothing feeds it to `grep -E`. So `\x00`/`\x7F` here are ECMAScript escapes, fully specified rather than implementation-dependent, and the negated class `[^\x00-\x7F]` means exactly 'any non-ASCII code unit'.

sightings: HIMMEL-2356 leg / PR #2070 — verified against a real suite marker line: bracket class no match, alternation match.
HIMMEL-2447 (this refresh) — the tree sweep's own first pattern returned a vacuous zero for exactly this reason; caught by a positive control.

classes.title: fenced code block without a language tag (markdownlint MD040)
classes.canonical: Open every fence with a language (`bash`, `text`, `json`, `mermaid`); CodeRabbit runs markdownlint-cli2 and files MD040 on each bare fence.
classes.coverage: No markdownlint in pre-commit; ~8 App re-raises since 2026-08-10 (MD040 + MD051 fragment links).

classes.title: new hook without a stated fail-open/fail-closed direction + bypass
classes.canonical: Decide by failure DIRECTION (scripts/hooks/CLAUDE.md): security fences fail closed; watchdogs and workflow nudges fail open on their own infrastructure errors. State it in the header, deny + name the exact replacement, and document the single-run bypass env var in the deny message.
classes.coverage: scripts/hooks/CLAUDE.md prose only. Ledger: scripts/hooks is the largest finding bucket (521 rows); 10 App re-raises on fail-open/closed since 2026-08-10.

classes.title: stub-fidelity / over-verification findings against a test fixture
classes.canonical: A fixture stub models only the behaviour under test; the suite asserts outcomes via marker files and captured output. 'The stub does not mimic X' is a finding only when X is on the path the case asserts — otherwise disprove, citing the assertion the case actually makes.
classes.coverage: cr-tune already clusters this bucket (test-fixture); no prompt-side carve-out existed before this entry. Ledger: the test-fixture bucket disproves at ~29% vs ~21% overall.

classes.title: doc-wording findings that contradict the implementing script
classes.canonical: A doc that states the implemented contract is not wrong because a reviewer expected another design, and parameterised paths (<state-repo>/…, $HANDOVER_DIR, C:/Users/<you>/…) are deliberately unresolvable here. Critic (diff only, no tools): raise a doc-vs-code contradiction only when the contradicting code is IN the diff, or the inconsistency is prose-vs-prose within the diff — cite both lines. Adjudicator: before agreeing, open the script the prose describes and agree only when you can cite the line it contradicts.
classes.coverage: .coderabbit.yaml docs/**/*.md instruction covers the parameterised-path half. Ledger: .md findings disprove at ~26% (43/165 adjudicated), .claude/commands/pr-check.md at ~28%.

classes.title: spawn-glm/spawn-claudex: plugin-profile resolution and failure teardown target the worker worktree, never the dispatcher
classes.canonical: Plugin-profile resolution in scripts/telegram/spawn-glm.ts and spawn-claudex.ts must run against the WORKER worktree, not the dispatcher's checkout — the dispatcher's profile answers the wrong question and masks worker-side misconfiguration. On a resolution failure, teardown is limited to a newly minted, owned profile directory; never remove a shared or pre-existing profile dir.
classes.coverage: CodeRabbit learnings only (top unmatched rows 2026-08-27: 55-use resolution row + 22-use teardown row). No shell-lint or .coderabbit.yaml rule covers this; detector would need TS AST awareness — left null, learning_match carries attribution.

classes.title: UTF-16 / BOM claims about scheduled-task XML in the schtasks emitter family
classes.canonical: These scripts drive Windows Task Scheduler through the schtasks CLI, not by hand-writing task XML. A finding of the form 'task XML is UTF-16, so this read/write/compare is broken' has been raised and DISPROVEN four separate times on this family (HIMMEL-2115). Disproof method, and the only one that counts: a LIVE Task Scheduler round-trip - register a task, read it back, including a non-ASCII path variant. The suite's fake scheduler stub is NOT evidence either way; it is precisely what makes the claim look plausible, so re-deriving the claim from the stub is not a new finding. Raise it only with a live round-trip that actually fails, and cite that run. SCOPE: this rebuttal covers the schtasks emitter family ONLY. Genuine encoding defects elsewhere still stand - notably NUL-byte / UTF-16 corruption truncating a scanned stream (HIMMEL-2194, a REAL leak-gate soundness hole). Never cite this class outside `globs`.
classes.coverage: Nothing structural enforces it: the emitters shell out to schtasks and the suite substitutes a stub, so neither the code nor the tests can refute the claim on their own - only a live round-trip can. Evidence: HIMMEL-2115 (PR #1991) burned four CR rounds re-disproving it on one branch. Filed as HIMMEL-2202.

hand_measured.note: hand-counted from the 28h leg report; evidence.ledger is left unset until --refresh mines it

classes.title: PR_CHECK_ANCHOR_DELEGATED handshake called forgeable => privilege escalation
classes.canonical: `pr-check-context.sh` reads its trust anchor from the environment: `anchor="${HIMMEL_REPO:-}"`. Any actor who can set `PR_CHECK_ANCHOR_DELEGATED` can equally set `HIMMEL_REPO=/attacker/checkout`, which redirects every anchor-side decision into attacker-controlled code BEFORE the handshake is ever consulted -- strictly weaker than an attack the actor can already mount, so forging the handshake grants no additional capability. A one-time unguessable token does not change this: the anchor process that would MINT the token is itself selected by `HIMMEL_REPO` -- against an environment-controlling actor, the attacker mints the token. The one shape that WOULD be a real escalation -- the repo under review injecting the variable without owning the launching shell -- is already closed: the script loads no `.env`, and its only `source` is `"$HIMMEL_ROOT/scripts/guardrails/lib.sh"`, where `HIMMEL_ROOT` derives from the script's own location and is fail-closed against not being a himmel checkout. SCOPE: this rebuts the ESCALATION premise only (forging the handshake gains capability). It does NOT cover the narrower, REAL residual -- the handshake binds to the anchor PATH only, not to (branch, head), so a STALE `PR_CHECK_ANCHOR_DELEGATED` surviving in the same shell is accepted at any branch/head and silently suppresses the delegation ledger row while still reporting `delegated=yes` (HIMMEL-2378, open). Raise that one with a concrete stale-value repro; do not re-raise this one.
classes.coverage: Raised 3 times across CR panel rounds on PR #2078 (HIMMEL-2335, branch fix/himmel-2335-prcheck-anchor: codex-2 12:13 / codex-4 14:05 / codex-1 19:29 on 2026-09-01, each 'forgeable because ... HIMMEL_REPO') plus once by the CodeRabbit App (its own added learning: 'an actor that controls the launching environment can replace the anchor through HIMMEL_REPO') -- every round disproved or deferred with this exact reasoning; the CodeRabbit round's own disposition deferred only the narrower stale-value residual to HIMMEL-2378.

hand_measured.note: hand-counted from .git/cr-critic-scores.jsonl and PR #2078's CodeRabbit App review comment; evidence.ledger is left unset until --refresh mines it

classes.title: CR-ledger availability rows claimed to need artifact/perspective scoping
classes.canonical: The availability supersession identity is (head, model) ONLY, and that is deliberate, not an oversight. ledger-append.sh states it inline (HIMMEL-1613): "availability is a property of the critic+commit pair, so a critic down at one head is down regardless of which review arm (artifact/perspective) probed it". Matching on those conjuncts was the BUG HIMMEL-1640 removed -- it left stale `unavailable` evidence alive when the `ok` came back on a different arm. clear-cr-marker.sh does the same plain last-write-wins per model, and any consumer that scopes differently would report an effective availability the GATE disagrees with, which is a harder failure to diagnose than the collision being alleged. Verify the cited code keys on (head, model) and mark disproved. SCOPE: this rebuts the availability claim only. The sibling claim about AMEND rows omitting branch is REAL and separately tracked (HIMMEL-2405) -- amend rows carry an empty `branch`, so that one cannot be fixed in a consumer either, but it is not this class.
classes.coverage: Raised twice on PR #2097 (HIMMEL-2321, branch fix/himmel-2321-runbook-twins): round 2 codex-2 and round 4 codex-1, both against scripts/cr/handover-bridge.sh, both disproved with the HIMMEL-1613/1640 reasoning above.

hand_measured.note: hand-counted from this branch panel rounds; evidence.ledger left unset until --refresh mines it

classes.title: test setup or child-process status unchecked — the suite cannot fail (vacuous green)
classes.canonical: A test whose SETUP can fail silently reports success for the wrong reason. Five shapes recur: (a) `TMP=$(mktemp -d ...)` with the status unchecked — on failure TMP is empty and every later "$TMP/x" path resolves to /x or the cwd; (b) a required tool (jq, node) assumed present, so the assertion never runs; (c) a child suite invoked with its exit status discarded, so a child that never completed reads as a pass; (d) a negative control whose else-branch is PASS with no error arm (`if grep -Eq "$p" <<<"$h"; then FAIL; else PASS; fi` folds grep status 2 — malformed ERE, unreadable input — into "absent"; branch 0 / 1 / anything else, and make the last a hard failure naming the status); (e) a hermetic PATH built from a hardcoded tool list is a stale snapshot — a later early dependency, or the assertion's own tool (cmp), is missing and the case exits command-not-found or on a same-rc early check, so reconcile the list against every binary reachable before the assertion. Check the setup and exit non-zero naming what was missing, and give every negative control a positive control proving the matcher can fire at all. This is the repo's own vacuous-verdict doctrine applied to test scaffolding: a zero from a probe you have not positive-controlled is not evidence.
classes.coverage: No structural check: shell-lint does not flag an unchecked mktemp assignment and .coderabbit.yaml has no instruction for it. 3 App raises in the measured window (2026-08-20..09-02) — unchecked mktemp/jq in a positive control, unchecked mktemp for TMP_ROOT, and check_hermetic ignoring a child suite's exit status. All three were legitimate. Shapes (d) and (e) folded in from HIMMEL-2648 (2026-09-21, HIMMEL-3339): ledger rows since 2026-09-04 — assert_not_matches reporting PASS for every nonzero grep status (adc611c), cmp absent from the hermetic HBIN list in test-uninstall.sh (01d38c7, a0f25eb; unadjudicated). No CodeRabbit-export row matches either shape and no deterministic detector exists (a single-line ADDED-line regex cannot see a branch's else arm or a tool list's reachability), so they extend this class instead of minting two prompt entries.

classes.title: an exit code gains a second meaning without its documented contract being updated
classes.canonical: Scripts here publish their exit codes in a header comment (`# Exit: 0 ok, 2 usage, ...`) and runbooks branch on them. When a change makes an existing code reachable by a second path, or adds a new one, the header AND every doc that branches on it move in the same commit — otherwise a caller keeps treating one code as one condition. State the full set of conditions for that code, not only the new one.
classes.coverage: No structural check; docs-flag-drift covers a removed --flag still documented, not an exit code whose MEANING widened. 2 App raises in the window: rc=21 documented only for a non-clean fence when a certification failure also returns it, and exit 5 gaining a second meaning in coderabbit-review.sh without its documented contract moving.

classes.title: Suggestion findings need a verdict for the marker gate even though they never enter blocking counts — the flow is documented
classes.canonical: Both facts are true at once and the runbooks already say so, so a finding that one contradicts the other rests on a false premise. Suggestions never enter the BLOCKING severity counts (a Suggestion-only round is 0 Critical / 0 Important), and they still require an explicit verdict, because clear-cr-marker.sh gate 4 refuses on ANY finding carrying an empty verdict regardless of severity — the panel writes its own rows with verdict:"". That was adjudicated as HIMMEL-2339 (option (a): the gate is right, the runbook sentence was aligned to it) after it cost a full round on #2057. Any of fixed / deferred / disproved is a valid disposition; a truthful `deferred` with a reason is the right answer for a real-but-out-of-scope suggestion.
classes.coverage: Documented in both /pr-check runbook twins after HIMMEL-2339 landed. 2 App raises on #2105 alone ('Define an adjudication flow for Suggestion findings', 'Amend Suggestion rows too'), plus the original round on #2057 — the class exists so a third PR does not pay for it.
